claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Inertial Electrostatic Confinement Fusion", series "Acquisition Threat Support", published 2010-03-10 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2009-12-01, DIA document number DIA-08-1003-006. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 72 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).
The DIA list transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018 opens with entry 1: 'Inertial Electrostatics Confinement Fusion, Dr George Miley, Univ. of Illinois.'
The released cover page carries the date 10 March 2010, an Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 1 December 2009 and document number DIA-08-1003-006; the author field is redacted under (b)(5).

claims.text: At 72 pages it is the longest single document in DIA's 37-document, 1,473-page FOIA release of 25 March 2022.
Puthoff named 'IEC fusion as a compact energy source' among the studies he commissioned, in his June 2018 Society for Scientific Exploration account of letting 38 contracts over a two-year period.

connections.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.
